steps.body: Meet the family. Any 4-sided shape is a **quadrilateral**. Two pairs of parallel sides make it a **parallelogram**. A parallelogram with 4 right angles is a **rectangle**; with 4 equal sides, a **rhombus**; with BOTH, a **square**. Each level keeps everything from its parent and adds one new attribute.

widget.prompt: Three corners are pinned. Move the tangerine fourth corner until the shape names itself a rectangle.
widget.successFeedback: You built a rectangle: opposite sides match, the diagonals match, and every corner is square. The name came from the attributes you constructed.
widget.sideFeedback: The moving corner is not aligned to make both pairs of opposite sides equal. Compare the live side lengths.
widget.angleFeedback: The opposite sides now match, but the corners are not all square. Use the right-angle marks and equal diagonals as evidence.

hints: Which attribute does it add: angles or sides?
Not all sides equal, so not square.
explanationVariants: Right angles without equal sides is a rectangle.
It takes the angle branch of the tree, not the side branch.

predict.prompt: Can a shape be BOTH a rectangle and a parallelogram at the same time?

options.label: Yes — every rectangle IS a parallelogram
No — it must be one or the other

predict.reveal: Shape families nest: a rectangle has two pairs of parallel sides, so it already qualifies as a parallelogram — one with right angles as a bonus.

cml.actionGoal: Construct a rectangle by coordinating opposite-side equality, diagonal equality, and right angles.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: Move the corner away from the target. Which single attribute breaks first, and how does the family name change?

explanation.prompt: Why does the finished shape belong to the rectangle family?

options.label: Its measured attributes force four right angles and equal opposite sides.
options.feedback: Exactly. The classification follows from invariant attributes, not how the drawing happens to look.

options.label: It looks like the rectangles I remember.
options.feedback: Appearance can mislead after a rotation or stretch. Use the live side, diagonal, and angle evidence.

steps.body: What makes a square a square?
explanationVariants: Equal sides is the extra attribute.

widget.prompt: Every square is a rectangle. What EXTRA attribute makes a square special among rectangles?

options.label: All four sides are equal
options.feedback: Right — equal sides is the square's addition to the rectangle package.

options.label: It has more right angles
options.feedback: Still exactly 4 — inherited from rectangles. The addition is equal SIDES.

options.label: Its opposite sides are parallel
options.feedback: Every rectangle already has that (inherited from parallelograms). The square's new attribute is equal sides.

hints: What do all rectangles already have?
Angles and parallel pairs come inherited.
The new thing is the sides.

steps.body: One cousin stands apart: the **trapezoid**, which in this course means **exactly one pair of parallel sides**. (Some books say "at least one pair" — we use "exactly one.") Under our definition, a trapezoid is never a parallelogram, and a parallelogram is never a trapezoid: two pairs is one too many.

explanationVariants: Two pairs breaks 'exactly one': not a trapezoid.
The definitions make the categories disjoint here.

widget.prompt: Using our definition (exactly one pair of parallel sides), is a parallelogram a trapezoid?

options.label: No — it has two pairs of parallel sides, one too many
Yes — it has parallel sides
options.feedback: That reads the definition as "at least one pair" — the other convention. Ours says EXACTLY one, so two pairs disqualifies it.

options.label: Only if its sides are equal
options.feedback: Side lengths aren't the test at all — the trapezoid definition counts parallel PAIRS, and a parallelogram has two.

hints: Count the parallel pairs, nothing else.
Exactly one means two is out.

widget.prompt: Each shape below is a parallelogram. Sort each one into the most specific family it belongs to.

items.label: Right angles, sides 6, 3, 6, 3
items.feedback: Right angles put it in the rectangle branch, and sides 6, 3, 6, 3 aren't all equal — so rectangle, not rhombus or square.

items.label: All sides 5, tilted corners
items.feedback: Four equal sides make it a rhombus; the tilted corners mean no right angles, so it can't be a rectangle or square.

items.label: Right angles, all sides 4
items.feedback: It has BOTH special attributes — right angles and equal sides — so the most specific family is square.

items.label: Sides 7, 4, 7, 4, tilted corners
items.feedback: Neither addition is present here — the corners are tilted and the sides come in two lengths — so it stays just a parallelogram.

widget.missFeedback: Check two things per shape: right angles? all sides equal? Angles alone → rectangle; sides alone → rhombus; both → square; neither → plain parallelogram.
widget.successFeedback: All four placed — you just walked the whole family tree.

explanationVariants: All four sides are 6, so the perimeter is 4 × 6 = 24.
The rhombus attribute (equal sides) makes the perimeter one multiplication.

widget.prompt: A rhombus has all sides equal to 6 units. What is its perimeter, in units?

commonErrors.feedback: 12 adds only two sides. A quadrilateral has four: 4 × 6 = 24.
6 is one side. Perimeter goes all the way around: 4 × 6 = 24.

hints: Test each claim against the tree.
A square has 4 equal sides — which family does that admit it to?
Equal sides is the rhombus attribute.
explanationVariants: Squares have 4 equal sides, so every square is a rhombus; the other claims fail on counterexamples.
Only the downward claim holds — a 5-by-2 rectangle and a tilted parallelogram sink the others.

widget.prompt: Exactly ONE of these claims is true. Which?

options.label: Every square is a rhombus
options.feedback: Right — a square has 4 equal sides, the rhombus attribute, so it belongs to that family too.

options.label: Every rectangle is a square
options.feedback: A 5-by-2 rectangle is the counterexample — its sides aren't all equal. Squares sit INSIDE rectangles, not the reverse.

options.label: Every parallelogram is a rectangle
options.feedback: A tilted parallelogram with no right angles is the counterexample. Rectangles are the parallelograms that ADD right angles.

takeaways: Quadrilateral → parallelogram → rectangle / rhombus → square; each level adds one attribute.
A square is both a rectangle and a rhombus — it has both additions.
Our trapezoid has exactly one parallel pair, so it sits outside the parallelogram branch.
steps.teaser: next: triangles — one shape, two family systems at once.

concept.body: Quick rewind. **Climb the ladder one attribute at a time.** Parallelogram (two parallel pairs) + right angles = rectangle. Parallelogram + equal sides = rhombus. A shape with both additions is a square. Ask: which addition does this shape have?

explanationVariants: Equal sides without right angles is the rhombus rung.
It made the sides addition, not the angles addition.

widget.prompt: A parallelogram has all sides equal but NO right angles. What is it?

options.label: A rhombus
options.feedback: Right — equal sides is the rhombus addition; no right angles keeps it out of the rectangle branch.

options.label: A square
options.feedback: A square needs right angles too. With tilted corners, equal sides alone makes a rhombus.

options.label: A rectangle
options.feedback: Rectangles are the right-ANGLE branch. This shape's addition is equal sides: rhombus.
